transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately, my mind has been feeling really foggy, and I just can't seem to focus or make decisions the way I used to. It's gotten to the point where even simple daily choices leave me feeling completely stuck, so I wanted to get some help.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or a lack of interest in activities you normally enjoy alongside these difficulties with focus and decision-making?

Yes, most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, like someone flipped a switch and drained all the color out of my life. I've also lost all interest in things I used to love, like sketching store layouts or working on my pottery, and now I usually just end up staring at them before going back to bed or watching TV.
How long have you been experiencing this heavy, sinking feeling and loss of interest in activities, was it a gradual change or did it start suddenly after a specific event?

This low period has been dragging on for about six months now, and it really started a few weeks after I began driving out to help my sister with her heart condition. Looking back, though, these big swings between feeling overly revved up and then completely drained have actually been coming and going for several years.
Can you describe these periods when you feel 'overly revved up' in more detail, such as what happens during those times and how they differ from your current state?

During those revved-up times, I felt incredibly upbeat and wired with endless energy, staying up late to reorganize my sister's house, take on extra consulting clients, and launch an online pottery shop, though I'd also easily snap at people and get highly distracted. I felt uniquely capable of fixing everything, which is the complete opposite of now, where I feel completely drained, foggy, and paralyzed by the simplest decisions.
Can you estimate how often these periods of feeling 'overly revved up' occurred and how long they typically lasted before you shifted back to feeling down or returning to a more normal state?

These big swings between feeling overly revved up and feeling drained have been coming and going for several years. I don't know the exact duration of each high period, but they always eventually gave way to these low, foggy phases. This current low stretch has been dragging on for about six months now.

Can you tell me more about the longest duration of one of your 'overly revved up' periods, and did you ever experience any periods where you felt relatively normal, without significant highs or lows, in between these episodes?

I'm not quite sure about the exact duration of my longest revved-up period, as I haven't really tracked them closely over the years. I also can't say for certain if I had completely normal periods in between, since it all feels a bit blurred when I look back.
Did your periods of feeling 'overly revved up' typically last for days, weeks, or even months at a time before shifting back to a low or more normal mood state?

Those revved-up periods typically last for a few weeks at a time. The most recent one lasted just a few weeks when I first started helping my sister, right before I crashed into this low state that has been going on for about six months now. Looking back, these ups and downs have been cycling like this for several years.
You mentioned snapping at people during your 'revved up' periods, can you tell me more about how often this happened and if you've experienced irritability during your current low period as well?

During those revved-up times, I would snap at people over the smallest things, especially if I felt they were slowing me down or getting in my way. Now, during this low period, I don't really feel irritable or snappy at all; instead, I just feel incredibly heavy, foggy, and completely drained.

Have you ever experienced a period where you felt both overly revved up and extremely low within a short span of time, like within a few days or a week, or have these mood swings always been more distinct and separate?

No, they have always been very distinct and separate rather than happening within a few days of each other. I had that highly energized, revved-up period when my sister first got sick, which then transitioned into this current low, foggy phase that has been dragging on for about six months. These separate swings have been coming and going like that for several years.
Can you confirm if you've had at least four mood episodes, either high or low, within the past 12 months, which would help clarify the pattern of your symptoms?
I'm not really sure of the exact number of episodes I've had in the last 12 months, as I haven't tracked them that closely. I just know that these swings have been coming and going over the years.
Can you try to estimate roughly how many times you've shifted between feeling overly revved up and extremely low in the past year, even if it's not an exact count?

I'm really not sure of the exact number of times I've shifted back and forth in the past year. These swings have been coming and going for several years, but this current low period has been dragging on for about the last six months.

Can you think of any way to approximate or recall roughly how many distinct episodes of feeling 'overly revved up' or 'extremely low' you've experienced in the past year, even if it's a wide range, to help us better understand the pattern of your symptoms?

Over the past year, I've really only experienced one major cycle: that highly energetic, revved-up phase when my sister first got sick, which then transitioned into this current low, foggy period that has been dragging on for about six months. While these types of swings have been coming and going for several years, this past year has mostly been defined by just this one transition from high to low.
Have you ever sought medical attention, been hospitalized, or experienced significant impairment in your daily life or relationships during either your 'revved up' or low periods?

I have never been hospitalized, but the impact on my daily life has been very real recently. I've had to turn down consulting projects, postpone work, and rely on my husband to handle our household tasks and bills. I finally decided to seek help after a longtime client pointed out how scattered my work had become, which led to my primary care doctor referring me to you.
During your 'overly revved up' periods, did you ever experience any psychotic symptoms, such as hearing voices or having delusional thoughts?

No, I have never experienced anything like hearing voices or having delusional thoughts during those high-energy periods. Even though my mind was racing and I felt very wired, I never lost touch with reality like that.

Can you confirm if you have experienced at least four distinct mood episodes, either manic/hypomanic or depressive, within a 12-month period at any point in your life, which might help differentiate between the diagnostic possibilities?

I'm not really sure and haven't tracked the exact number of episodes within a single year. While these ups and downs have been coming and going for several years, I don't know if I've ever had as many as four distinct shifts in one 12-month period.

Can you think back over the entire course of your illness and estimate the total number of distinct episodes, either high or low, you've experienced over the years, as this might help clarify the pattern of your symptoms?
I'm really not sure of the exact number of episodes because I've never kept an official count. I just know that these high and low swings have been coming and going for several years now.

Can you recall if there was ever a year where you experienced more frequent shifts between your high and low periods, even if you can't pinpoint the exact number of episodes, to help differentiate between possible diagnoses?
I can't recall a specific year when the shifts were more frequent than usual. These swings between feeling revved up and drained have just been coming and going for several years now.

Can you consider keeping a mood journal for the next few months to track the frequency and duration of your high and low periods, which might help clarify the pattern of your symptoms and guide our diagnosis?
I'd be open to trying that. I've never kept a mood journal or tracked my feelings like that before, but it sounds like a helpful way to make sense of these shifts.
In your experience, have you typically had more than four mood episodes, either high or low, within a single year at any point in your life?
I don't think I've ever had them that frequently in a single year. My high and low periods usually seem to last longer than that, so four shifts in one year doesn't sound like my typical pattern.
Can you definitively say that you have never experienced more than four distinct mood episodes, either manic/hypomanic or depressive, within a 12-month period throughout your entire life?

I can't say definitively because I've never kept a close count of my episodes over the years. I just know for sure that these swings between feeling highly energized and feeling completely drained have been coming and going for several years.

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt overly revved up and met the criteria for a manic episode, such as needing less sleep, feeling more talkative, or engaging in risky behaviors?

Yes, I've had periods like that lasting a few weeks where I felt incredibly wired and upbeat, staying up late to work on projects because I had endless energy and felt highly confident in my abilities. During those times, I would take on far too many tasks and get easily distracted, constantly jumping from one thing to another. These episodes of feeling highly driven and energized have occurred on and off for several years now.
During your 'overly revved up' periods, did you ever engage in impulsive or risky behaviors, such as excessive spending, reckless driving, or impulsive sexual behavior?

No, I don't recall engaging in any risky behaviors like reckless driving, excessive spending, or impulsive sexual behavior during those times. My high-energy periods were really just focused on working late, taking on too many projects, and reorganizing things.

Can you think of any significant events, stressors, or triggers that might have preceded or followed your shifts between feeling 'overly revved up' and 'extremely low', which could help us understand the pattern of your symptoms?

The most significant trigger recently was my older sister being diagnosed with a chronic heart condition. Taking on her caregiving and the weekend travel initially triggered that highly energized, revved-up phase, but the constant juggling and lack of sleep eventually caused me to crash into this current low, foggy state. While these shifts have happened on and off for several years, her illness was the clear trigger for this latest cycle.
Can you confirm whether the current six-month low period is the longest you've experienced, or have you had longer periods of feeling low in the past?

I'm not entirely sure if I've had low periods that lasted longer than this current six-month stretch. Since these swings have been coming and going for several years, I can't quite remember the exact length of the past ones compared to this one.

Can you try to recall if there was ever a period in your life where you experienced a higher frequency of mood episodes, either high or low, that might have lasted for a shorter duration, such as a few months, to help differentiate between possible diagnoses?

I don't recall ever having a period where the swings were much faster or more frequent than what I've experienced. For me, they have typically lasted for months at a time and have been coming and going like that for several years.

Can you confirm if your 'overly revved up' periods have ever met the full criteria for a manic episode, including needing less sleep, feeling more talkative than usual, or engaging in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences, and have these episodes significantly impacted your daily life or relationships?

During those high-energy times, I would stay up half the night working and felt like I didn't need much sleep, but I don't recall being unusually talkative or doing risky things with painful consequences. Those 'up' phases actually felt highly productive and didn't cause major problems in my life or relationships, other than occasionally snapping at people when they slowed me down, which is very different from how much my current low period is disrupting my life.

Can you confirm whether your 'overly revved up' periods have ever lasted for at least four consecutive days, meeting the criteria for hypomanic episodes, and if so, how they have impacted your daily functioning and relationships?

Yes, those high-energy periods definitely lasted longer than four days, often stretching out for weeks during my swings over the years. They impacted my functioning because I’d stay up all night, pack my schedule with too many projects, and constantly jump between unfinished tasks. In my relationships, I would snap at anyone who slowed me down and even boast to friends that I was the only one who could really handle everything.

Can you estimate how many distinct episodes of either feeling overly revved up or extremely low you've experienced in total over the course of your illness, to help clarify the pattern of your symptoms?
I'm not sure of the exact number of episodes because I've never kept a precise count of them. I just know that these ups and downs have been coming and going for several years now.
Can you confirm if you've had more episodes of hypomania or more episodes of major depression over the course of your illness?

I'm really not sure which type of episode has occurred more often over the years. I just know that these swings between feeling highly energized and feeling very drained and foggy have been coming and going for several years now.

Can you try to recall if the pattern of your mood episodes, either high or low, has been consistently cyclical over the years, or if there have been periods where the episodes were less frequent or more spaced out?

I'm not entirely sure whether there was a consistent cycle or if they were more spaced out over the years. I just know that these ups and downs have been coming and going for several years now, with this most recent stretch being clearly triggered by my sister's illness.
